name: Ploče
title: Ploče Bulk Carrier Gauging | UTM for Holds and Hatch Covers
description: Thickness measurement at Ploče for bulk carriers, general cargo and tankers: ultrasonic gauging of holds, hatch covers, tank tops and decks at the Neretva port.
h1: Ploče Port: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement for Bulk and Cargo Ships
intro: Ploče is the deep-water port at the mouth of the Neretva, and the main sea outlet for Bosnia and Herzegovina as well as southern Croatia. Bulk carriers, general cargo ships and tankers work its quays on a steady schedule of discharge and loading. Atlantis NDT mobilises ultrasonic gauging technicians from India to the ship, to measure holds, hatch covers, tank tops and decks during cargo stops or at anchor.

highlights.h: A working bulk and cargo port
highlights.p: Ploče handles dry bulk, general cargo, timber and liquid cargo, so the same visit can reach bulk carriers whose holds are open after discharge and product tankers with accessible decks.

highlights.h: The outlet for Bosnia and Herzegovina
highlights.p: Cargo moving to and from the Bosnian interior runs through Ploče by rail and road, which gives the port regular bulk and general cargo calls and a predictable demand for hold and hatch cover gauging.
The port suits bulk ships and discharge-stage gauging, but heavy repair and docking take place elsewhere on the Adriatic, so Ploče work is mostly condition checks and pre-docking estimates.

port.h: The port of Ploče, the Neretva delta and the approach
p: Ploče was built in the twentieth century as a modern deep-water port on the Adriatic coast, on a sheltered bay near the mouth of the Neretva River. The port authority manages the quays, terminals and storage areas, and the town grew around the harbour. Behind the port the Neretva delta stretches inland, a low-lying agricultural area, while the mountains rise sharply further back. The approach from the Adriatic passes the Pelješac peninsula, and the sea route runs through relatively sheltered water between the peninsula and the mainland, so ships reach the port without long exposed passages.

Traffic reflects the economic geography. Ploče is the nearest Croatian deep-water port to much of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and cargo flows through the port by rail and road to the interior. Dry bulk such as coal, ores, grain, fertiliser and aggregates is common, alongside general cargo, timber, containers and steel products. A liquid cargo terminal receives tankers carrying petroleum products and other liquids. Bulk carriers are the dominant ship type here, usually of handysize or handymax scale, and the pattern of loading and discharging creates regular windows where holds are empty and accessible for gauging. Tankers and general cargo ships make up much of the rest.

Berths are allocated by the port authority and the terminal operators, and ships sometimes wait at anchor off the port when quays are busy. The anchorage is reasonably sheltered, although the bora can blow strongly across the delta and the coast, and the jugo brings swell and rain in winter. The tidal range is small, so ship movement alongside is minimal. Dust control, cargo handling schedules and weather all influence working windows on bulk berths, and gauging has to be planned with the terminal and the agent so that technicians work in clean, safe holds without interrupting loading or discharge.

Most gauging at Ploče takes place alongside. A bulk carrier that has finished discharge offers open holds, hopper tank tops, hatch covers and coamings, and with the cargo gone the surfaces can be cleaned enough for readings. The ship's crew or the terminal's cleaning gang usually prepares the hold, and the technicians work in the gap between discharge and the next loading. For hold frames and side shell structure, staging or lifting equipment is arranged with the ship's staff, and enclosed-space entry procedures apply throughout.

Ploče is not a repair port, and we do not assume docking capacity. Ships needing a docking survey normally sail to a yard elsewhere in Croatia, Italy, Montenegro or further afield. Gauging at Ploče is therefore valuable as a pre-docking step: measured thicknesses help the owner and the yard prepare a steel estimate, and the surveyor can focus the close-up survey on areas where corrosion is most likely. Ships waiting at anchor off the port can be reached by launch through the agent, which suits pre-purchase and condition checks.

General cargo quays — hold structure, hatch covers and deck plating on break-bulk and timber ships
Liquid cargo terminal — main deck, deck piping and accessible ballast tanks on product tankers during discharge
Container berths — hatch covers and ballast tanks on feeder ships during cargo work

context.h: Regulation, bulk carrier survey rules and the Bosnian trade
p: Foreign ships at Ploče are subject to Paris MoU port state control, carried out by Croatian officers under the Ministry of the Sea, Transport and Infrastructure and the harbour master's authority for the Ploče area. Bulk carriers are a recurring target for structural inspections because of the damage hold frames, hopper tank boundaries and hatch covers suffer from grabs and cargo. Ageing handysize ships trading in the Adriatic are the kind of tonnage where measured values matter, because a ship with substantial corrosion in a hold can be required to carry out steel renewal before she is allowed to continue.

Bulk carriers fall under the enhanced survey programme, with thickness measurement at special and intermediate surveys and increasing coverage as the ship ages. Owners trading to Ploče often gauge selected holds and hatch covers between surveys to manage the risk of findings. EU rules add further layers: larger ships need an Inventory of Hazardous Materials, and EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime apply above the size thresholds. The cargo mix, dominated by coal, ores and aggregates in many cases, tends to be abrasive, so wastage in the lower hold areas and tank tops is often the key finding for older ships.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Ploče
jobs.p: Ploče jobs revolve around bulk carriers and discharge windows. A ship that has just emptied a hold can have the structure measured before the next loading, and an owner can use the same stop to check hatch covers and ballast tanks. We agree scope, access method and report format with the superintendent before the team travels from India, and plan around the terminal's operating hours.
list: Hold frame and tank top gauging on a handysize bulk carrier after discharge, with readings located by frame number
Hatch cover panel and coaming gauging on a general cargo ship before her intermediate survey
Hopper and topside tank readings on a bulk carrier at anchor, in preparation for a docking survey elsewhere
Main deck and deck piping gauging on a product tanker discharging at the liquid cargo terminal, with ballast tanks added if certified for entry
Pre-purchase condition gauging of a coaster at anchor off Ploče, reached by launch through the agent

logistics: Dubrovnik Airport is the nearest international airport, with Split further north and Mostar in Bosnia and Herzegovina also within road distance. The agent arranges port access and terminal passes, and books launches for ships at anchor. Technicians travelling from India need a Schengen visa for Croatia, and the visa timing governs the earliest start. Bulk berth schedules change with cargo flow, so we keep dates flexible and confirm the working window with the terminal once the ship is alongside.

faqs.q: Can holds be gauged during discharge at Ploče?
faqs.a: Usually only after discharge, once the hold is empty and has been swept or cleaned. Gauging then has to fit between the end of discharge and the start of loading. The crew prepares the hold and enclosed-space entry procedures apply, so we agree the timing with the terminal and the ship's officers beforehand.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock at Ploče for a docking survey?
faqs.a: Ploče is a cargo port, and we do not assume docking capacity. Ships that need a docking normally sail to a yard in Croatia, Italy or elsewhere. We gauge at Ploče beforehand, so the yard has a steel estimate and the surveyor can focus on the areas most likely to need work.

faqs.q: Can hatch covers be gauged while the ship is alongside?
faqs.a: Yes. Hatch cover panels and coamings can be measured when the covers are open or stowed, subject to safe access and the terminal's rules. Readings are recorded by panel and position, which helps the owner decide which panels need repair before the next survey.

faqs.q: Can a ship at anchor off Ploče be gauged?
faqs.a: Yes, through a launch arranged by the agent. Anchorage work suits pre-purchase, on-hire, off-hire and pre-docking checks. Weather can interrupt boat transfers, particularly in strong bora, so the plan includes a spare day, and tanks need to be gas-free and certified for entry.
